title: Gene Norman's Just Jazz concerts recorded without musicians' awareness
summary: Callender says he knew the concerts were taped but never thought of commercial release; they try to recall venues and drummer.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: On Dial. Martha Glaser asked to ask you: You knew you were being recorded at Gene Norman's Just Jazz concerts, and you said you didn't think about those things, you were just playing and you didn't notice. Right?

Yeah. I really didn't notice. I knew they had...what was it, a wire recorder or tape recorder set up, but I didn't think about it being for commercial reasons. But later, it did turn out to be commercial.
And I met one guy I forgot to mention. Jack McVea was a part of that. I can't remember the drummer. Maybe a guy named Tucker or something. I really can't remember. But yes, I remember...
Well, there was a drummer named Henry Tucker.
Well, yeah, he was on some of those. Because we played in an auditorium...was it the Embassy or maybe something...
Gene I don't think used the Embassy. He used the Pasadena and the Shrine, and... I don't remember him using the Embassy.
Well, anyhow, we played several places, and I know Gene did a lot of recording. I didn't think about them being released as records at the time. But yes...
Martha was interested in knowing whether the musicians were aware that it was being taken down at the time that it happened.
